results.title: Field results, Wolaita 2025
results.intro: 17 indicators recorded with farmers in Offa Woreda, Wolaita, South Ethiopia. Each prediction was compared with historical recorded weather and given a preliminary score out of 10.
results.trustRule: Very strong is a score of 9 or more, strong is 8 to 8.9, fair is 7 to 7.9, and weak is below 7.
results.methodField: The 17 field scores are preliminary. The Sign & Sky AI compared each farmers' prediction with historical recorded weather for Wolaita, but the rainfall data behind these scores were not kept, so they cannot be checked yet. They are stored as recorded and marked “field-ai-2025”. A reproducible re-test with CHIRPS satellite rainfall and ERA5, with every prediction fixed in advance, is under way.
results.methodNew: New tests use a published, repeatable method (sns-score-v1). A sign seen on day D predicts an outcome within W days. The tool takes daily rainfall for the W days after D, and for the same calendar window in each of the N earlier years (10 by default).
results.formulaH: H is 1 if the predicted outcome happened in the window, otherwise 0.
results.formulaP: P is where this year's window ranks among the earlier years (0 to 1), turned toward the prediction: wetter counts for rain signs, drier for dry signs.
results.datasets: Data: ERA5 reanalysis through the Open-Meteo Historical Weather API, and CHIRPS daily rainfall once its extractor is connected. Every test keeps the request, the daily values, the thresholds and the calculation.
results.thresholds: Rain happened: at least 10 mm in the window. Heavy rain: one day of 20 mm or more. Start of the rains: 3 days totalling 20 mm with at least 2 wet days. Normal: between the 25th and 75th percentile. Dry: under 5 mm or under half the usual amount. Drought: at or below the 20th percentile.

about.title: About Sign & Sky
about.lead: Farmers have read the sky, the trees and the animals for generations. Sign & Sky records those signs, tests each one against recorded weather, and gives the result back to farmers in their own language.
promises: Every sign stays credited to the community it came from. Farmers' names and villages are never published.
Every score shows how it was made: the data, the years compared and the calculation.
A weak score is said plainly. We never call a sign reliable when the data does not support it.
how: Listen: the farmer speaks or types a sign.
Understand: Sign & Sky recognises the sign and reads the place and season.
Test: the sign's score against recorded weather is looked up, or the sign is saved for testing.
Voice advice: the answer is spoken and written.
about.seasonsEthiopia: Belg (short rains): March–May. Kiremt / Meher (main rains): June–September. Bega (dry season): October–February.
about.placesText: Every sign in Sign & Sky was recorded with farmers in Offa Woreda, Wolaita Zone, South Ethiopia, and every score refers to rainfall in Wolaita.
about.dataText: Recorded weather comes from ERA5 reanalysis and, when connected, CHIRPS satellite rainfall.
about.apiText: The published library, in both languages with every test result, is open at {url} for apps such as the offline Sign & Sky Android app.

source.title: Where the knowledge comes from
source.lead: The 17 signs come from a 2025 survey of 283 farming households in three kebeles of Offa Woreda, Wolaita, South Ethiopia, together with interviews of knowledgeable farmers and group discussions. Many farmers named the same signs, so each sign was recorded once: this is knowledge the whole community shares.
source.doc: Traditional Knowledge Systems & Microclimate Indicators — Indigenous Weather Forecasting, Wolaita, South Ethiopia
steps: Observed

In 2025, 283 household heads in three randomly chosen kebeles of Offa Woreda were surveyed, and knowledgeable farmers took part in interviews and group discussions. They described the signs they read in nature: ants, birds, squirrels and frogs, the wind, the sun, moon and stars, clouds, mist and flowering trees.
Recorded

Signs named by many farmers were recorded once. Each sign was written into the field table with seven fields: the indicator, the behaviour seen, its meaning in local knowledge, the place, the date, whether it was tested with scientific data, and its score.
Tested
Each sign's prediction was compared with historical recorded rainfall for Wolaita by the Sign & Sky AI.
Scored
Every sign received a preliminary score from 0 to 10. A reproducible re-test with CHIRPS satellite rainfall and ERA5, with each prediction fixed in advance, is under way.
Returned
The result goes back to farmers as spoken and written advice in English and Amharic.

landing.tagline: Nature Has Its Own Language. We Help You Understand It.
landing.taglineText: Connecting indigenous weather knowledge with satellite observations and climate intelligence to support agricultural decisions.

how.title: From a sign in nature to advice you can use
steps: Farmers observe
Farmers notice signs in nature: ants, birds, wind, clouds, the sun, moon and stars.
Knowledge is documented
Each sign is recorded with its meaning, place and date, in the farmers' own words.
Data are joined
Satellite and climate records for the same place and dates are brought in: CHIRPS, ERA5 and GI-AI4AFS.
The sign is tested
The prediction is compared with what the weather actually did, and with what chance alone would give.
Evidence returns
The result goes back to farmers as a score and spoken advice in their language, weak signs included.

mission.title: Our mission and approach
items: Give farmers trustworthy weather advice in their own language by testing the signs they already read against satellite and climate data.
A living, open record of indigenous weather knowledge across Ethiopia, where every sign has an honest track record and farmers and scientists learn from each other.

Farmers decide when to prepare land, plant and protect their harvest partly from signs in nature. National forecasts cover wide areas and often arrive late; local knowledge is immediate, but rarely tested.
Each sign is checked against CHIRPS satellite rainfall (since 1981), ERA5 reanalysis and, once access is granted, Sentinel-2 vegetation data from the GI-AI4AFS spatio-temporal API.

AI understands what farmers say in English and Amharic, extracts the matching satellite and climate data for the place and dates, joins it with the stored indigenous record, runs the test and speaks the answer back. People review every new sign before it is published.

Predictions are fixed in writing before the data are seen, scores are compared with what a sign with no skill would earn, and every number can be reproduced from open code and public data. The 2025 scores are preliminary until the re-test is published.
Offa Woreda in Wolaita Zone, South Ethiopia: two rainy seasons (Belg and Kiremt) and smallholder farms built around enset, maize and other crops.
Add Wolaytta, release the offline Android app, build multi-season track records for each sign, extend to other zones, and combine proven signs with official seasonal forecasts.
mission.teamTeaser: The farmers' knowledge is at the centre; the team builds the tools around it.

environment.title: Environmental intelligence
environment.lead: Every Sign & Sky test joins a farmer's sign with the satellite and climate record for the same place and dates. These are the sources, and where each one stands today.

sources.name: CHIRPS v2.0
sources.what: Satellite and rain-gauge rainfall, daily, about 5 km, since 1981 (Climate Hazards Center).
sources.use: The primary rainfall record for the research re-test of the 17 signs.

sources.name: ERA5 reanalysis (via Open-Meteo)
sources.what: Reanalysis rainfall, daily, about 25 km, since 1940 (Copernicus Climate Change Service).
sources.use: Runs the weather tests that researchers start from this website, and checks the CHIRPS results.

sources.name: GI-AI4AFS Spatio-Temporal API
sources.what: Sentinel-2 imagery and vegetation indices (NDVI, NDMI, EVI) as map tiles and time series (STAC and OGC standards).
sources.use: AI will extract the vegetation and land data for each observation's place and dates and join it with the indigenous record.

study: Offa Woreda centre: 6.75° N, 37.50° E (primary test point)
Seasons: Belg March–May, Kiremt June–September, Bega October–February

environment.honesty: Data are never invented: where a source is not yet connected, this page says so.

calendar.title: Seasonal calendar
calendar.lead: Wolaita has two rainy seasons. The short Belg rains start the planting, the long Kiremt rains carry the main Meher cropping season, and Bega is the dry season. Each marker is a sign farmers saw on that date in 2025.

belg: Short rains: land preparation and early planting.
kiremt: Main rains: the main cropping season.
bega: Dry season: harvest, drying and storage.

stories.title: Wisdom Written in Nature
stories.lead: For generations, farmers in Wolaita have read the coming season in ants, birds, winds and stars. This is what they shared in 2025, with the meanings they gave.
stories.consentText: We publish farmers' own stories, photos and recordings only with their consent and in their own words. If you farm in Wolaita and want to share a sign or a story, use Share a sign.
